title.narrative: Enhancing Export Readiness of Women and Youth-led MSMEs within the AfCFTA, Leveraging Digital Technologies

description.narrative: Despite its position as Africa’s largest economy, accounting for more than 15% of the continent’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP), and a population exceeding 200 million, Nigeria struggles to leverage its strengths to benefit from regional trade and integration. This challenge is evident in the significantly low intra-African trade volumes, which stood at only 4.5 percent in 2022. Harnessing the country’s immense potential will require the strengthening of local production value chains, policies, infrastructure, and adoption of digital technologies, especially for populations at risk of exclusion such as women and youth.The Africa Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) offers to create a single market for goods and services within the continent and seeks to provide untapped opportunities for African economies to increase intra-regional trade by progressively eliminating 90% of tariffs on intra-regional trade, leading to a reduction in the cost of trade and improvement in competition and productivity. This is expected to yield improved incomes and drive economy growth. Nigeria stands to benefit from these opportunities by strengthening its trade capacity, boosting domestic production of competitive goods and services and prioritizing women and youth MSMEs as drivers of trade. The Agreement provides an opportunity to unlock growth and increase output in Nigeria’s untapped sectors such as tourism and fashion. In addition, it can lead to the transformation of other industries such as petrochemicals, creating potential for increased revenue and trade output.UNDP Nigeria aims to support the government of Nigeria to achieve these development outcomes by strengthening institutional capacities of the government, building the capacity of women and youth MSMEs to trade, and facilitating trading activities through business-to-business linkages as well as supporting the liberalization of trade across prioritized value-chains.
